Command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the sin offering in a holy place
Summary: The command: Priests shall eat the flesh of the sin offering in a holy place (Leviticus 6:26). The priest who offered the sin offering ate its flesh in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle.
Commandment: Priests shall eat the flesh of the sin offering in a holy place, as prescribed in Leviticus 6:26.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. Hebrews teaches these sacrifices could never perfect the worshiper; they pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering, which is why they ceased with the new covenant.
Purpose: To provide atonement, thanksgiving, and fellowship under the old covenant. Hebrews teaches these pointed forward to Christ's once-for-all offering (Hebrews 10:1-14), so the system ceased.
Function: The priest who offered the sin offering ate its flesh in the holy place, in the court of the tabernacle — a ceremonial law about holy food. Its goal was to keep the sin offering's flesh within the sanctuary, eaten by the priest who bore the people's guilt in the rite. It did not address a particular evil; its work was order in worship, not restraint. The holy meal stayed in the holy place, and the priest's portion was part of the atonement's work.
